neighbours.label: Soviet-bloc Cold War history: names and entities (Khrushchev, Sino-Soviet, Yugoslavia, Warsaw Pact)
fire: After Stalin's death, Khrushchev launched a campaign of de-Stalinization.
Relations soured during the Sino-Soviet border clashes of 1969.
Brezhnev ordered Warsaw Pact troops into Czechoslovakia in 1968.
The collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991 ended the Cold War.
Tito broke with Moscow and led Yugoslavia on its own path.
Gorbachev's reforms loosened Moscow's grip on Eastern Europe.
The Hungarian uprising of 1956 was crushed by Soviet tanks.
In 1961 East German authorities began building the Berlin Wall.
quiet: After Napoleon's defeat, the Congress of Vienna redrew the map of Europe.
Relations soured during the Anglo-French border disputes of the 1700s.
Caesar ordered his legions across the Rubicon in 49 BC.
The collapse of the Roman Empire in 476 ended an era in the west.
Henry VIII broke with Rome and led England on its own path.
Bismarck's reforms strengthened his grip on the German states.
The peasant uprising of 1381 was crushed by royal troops.
In 1889 French engineers began building the Eiffel Tower.

notes: Probe: Khrushchev 0.66, Sino-Soviet 0.46. The + pole is the Vietnam War (Viet Cong, North/South).
